title: My WhatsApp was hacked: what you can do now
pageTitle: My WhatsApp was hacked: what you can do now | Spamlock
description: Someone got into your WhatsApp? Steps you can take now: sign back in with your 6-digit code, warn your friends, log out unknown devices and turn on two-step verification.
answer: Sign back in to WhatsApp on your phone with the 6-digit code it sends you. This logs everyone else out. Changing a password doesn’t. Then warn your family and friends.
stepsTitle: Steps you can take if your WhatsApp was hacked

steps.title: Sign back in with the 6-digit code
steps.text: Open WhatsApp on your phone and sign in again with your number. WhatsApp sends you a 6-digit code by text or call. Once you enter it, anyone else using your account is logged out.

steps.title: Never share the 6-digit code
steps.text: Not even with family or friends. Whoever has the code can take your account.

steps.title: Asked for a PIN you never set?
steps.text: The other person may have set it. If you don’t know it, WhatsApp says to wait 7 days and try again.

steps.title: Get back in before you report it
steps.text: WhatsApp says reporting the account you’re trying to recover could get it banned, and you could lose it.

steps.title: Warn your family and friends
steps.text: Whoever got in can pretend to be you in chats and groups. You can ask them to ignore requests for money or codes sent from your account.

steps.title: Log out devices you don’t know
steps.text: In WhatsApp, open Linked Devices. Tap any device you don’t recognise, then Log Out.

steps.title: Turn on two-step verification
steps.text: You’ll find it in WhatsApp’s Account settings. You choose a password, so the 6-digit code alone isn’t enough to get into your account.

app.title: Check links in the Spamlock app
app.text: Check any link or QR code before you open it.
